response.passage: Q: Why do we need to wash our hands even if they look clean? A: Germs are microscopic organisms that are invisible to the naked eye, so hands can carry harmful pathogens even when they appear perfectly clean. Q: Is rinsing with water enough to remove germs? A: No, soap is essential because it breaks down the oily layer on your skin that traps germs, allowing them to be rinsed away effectively. Q: How should we behave when we have a cough? A: Always cover your mouth with a tissue or your bent elbow, never your bare palm, because germs can easily transfer from your hand to surfaces you touch later. Q: Do antibiotics help with every illness? A: No, antibiotics are specifically designed to kill bacteria; they have no effect on viruses that cause common colds or the flu. Q: How do we make water safe to drink? A: Simply filtering water through a cloth is not enough to remove tiny pathogens; you must boil water vigorously for at least one minute to ensure all harmful germs are destroyed.
response.summary: This passage explains that germs are invisible and require soap for proper removal. It also clarifies that coughing etiquette, correct water purification, and the specific use of antibiotics are vital for maintaining health.
